old_title: ABC wins scoop of the year at 2026 Walkley Awards
new_title: ABC wins scoop of the year at 2026 Walkley Awards
old_text:
In short:
The ABC has won seven Walkley awards this year, including scoop of the year.
ABC radio, television and digital journalism has been recognised.
The Walkley Foundation's chief executive said public interest journalism was in good hands.
The ABC has won seven gongs at this year's Walkley Awards, including the coveted Scoop of the Year prize for coverage of ASIO's failures ahead of the Bondi terrorist attack.
The 71st Walkley Awards for Excellence in Journalism was hosted in Sydney, Thursday night, with 30 categories.
The Walkley Foundation's chief executive, Shona Martyn said: "Once again the Walkley Awards have proved the excellence and breadth of Australian journalism."
"Public interest journalism is in good hands with these Australian journalists who are working against a backdrop of challenges to journalism, press freedom and news organisations in a shifting world."
Full list of ABC Walkley winners
All media: Scoop of the year
Sean Rubinsztein-Dunlop, Olivia Caisley, Michael Workman, ABC Investigations, ABC News Online, 7.30, Bondi: What ASIO knew
All media: International
Stephanie March, Naomi Selvaratnam, Leah Donovan - with Shrouq Ali and Jaber Badwan (Gaza), Foreign Correspondent, 'Gaza Children of War'
Radio/Audio short (under 20 mins)
Hamish Macdonald, Mark Tobin, Jemima Huston, Georgie Carroll, 702 Sydney Mornings, Gendered violence against women in Australian politics
Radio/Audio long (over 20 mins)
Andy Burns, Charlotte King with Background Briefing and Regional Investigations team, Background Briefing, Hometown Boys
Digital media: Innovation journalism
ABC Digital Story Innovations Team, ABC News Online, This is what 84 cameras reveal about the Bondi attack
Television/Video: News reporting
Bridget Rollason, ABC News, ISIS brides return to Australia
Television/Video: Current affairs long (over 20 mins)
Dylan Welch, Elise Potaka, Amy Greenbank, Four Corners, Brutal Force
Investigative Journalism
For the second time, The Age's Nick McKenzie took home the Gold Walkley.
Nick McKenzie's investigation into Mick Gatto and the CFMEU found that Victoria's Labor government had been repeatedly warned about union misconduct and alleged criminal infiltration of the state's construction sector.
The piece helped Mr McKenzie walk out with the award for the Investigative Journalism category, bringing his tally of Walkley awards throughout his career to 22.
Press Photographer of the Year
Jason Edwards was named the Press Photographer of the Year for his portfolio of work for the Herald Sun.
"It is a testament to the fact that, despite challenges, Australian journalists are producing work of great public interest, originality and courage." said Gay Alcorn, chair of the Walkley judging board.
new_text:
In short:
Nick McKenzie has taken out the top gong for Australian journalism at the Walkley awards.
The ABC won seven awards, including scoop of the year.
The Walkley Foundation's chief executive said public interest journalism was in good hands.
The ABC has won seven gongs at this year's Walkley Awards, including the scoop of the year prize.
Nine newspaper journalist Nick McKenzie took out the highest accolade in Australian journalism, the Gold Walkley.
The 71st Walkley Awards for Excellence in Journalism were hosted in Sydney last night, with 30 categories.
McKenzie was awarded the Gold Walkley for his investigation into Victorian underworld figure Mick Gatto, and how the Victorian Labor government allowed wrongdoing to occur on its $100 billion infrastructure program, Big Build.
McKenzie also won the investigative journalism category for that story, bringing his tally of Walkley awards throughout his career to 22.
The judging board described it as "truth-to-power journalism in the face of attempts to shut him down with actual violence".
"It's not just a Victorian story, it speaks to our nation and the way our democracy works. Tenacious reporting presented in accessible ways, instrumental in bringing down a government," it said.
The ABC took out the coveted scoop of the year for coverage of ASIO's failures ahead of the Bondi terrorist attack.
Sean Rubinsztein-Dunlop, Olivia Caisley and Michael Workman were given the award for their story Bondi: What ASIO Knew, produced for ABC Investigations, ABC News Online and 7.30.
The Walkley Foundation chief executive Shona Martyn said this year's award showed the "excellence and breadth of Australian journalism".
"Public interest journalism is in good hands with these Australian journalists who are working against a backdrop of challenges to journalism, press freedom and news organisations in a shifting world," Ms Martyn.
List of Walkley winners

Print/text: feature writing short
Sam Buckingham-Jones, Australian Financial Review, 'Maccas in a Rolls: Inside Kyle Sandilands' pivot to $100 tradie plans'
All media: coverage of indigenous affairs
Ben Smee & the Guardian Australia team, Guardian Australia, the betrayal of kardell lomas
Radio/Audio short (under 20 mins)
Hamish Macdonald, Mark Tobin, Jemima Huston, Georgie Carroll, ABC 702 Sydney Mornings, Gendered violence against women in Australian politics.
Radio/Audio long (over 20 mins)

All media: Scoop of the year
Sean Rubinsztein-Dunlop, Olivia Caisley, Michael Workman, ABC Investigations, ABC News Online, 7.30, Bondi: What ASIO knew.
All media: International
Stephanie March, Naomi Selvaratnam, Leah Donovan - with Shrouq Ali and Jaber Badwan (Gaza), Foreign Correspondent, Gaza Children of War.
